subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model evals and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Schmidt <a.schmidt@globexretail.de>, Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@apaccommerce.co.sg>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (multilingual evals)

Hi Anna / Ravi --

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and our proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goal: Improve customer support automation across EU (DE/FR/ES/IT) and APAC (JP/KR/SG) markets while keeping latency under 300ms median for chat flows and avoiding regressions vs your current SparkHelp model.
- Key risk you called out: German & French formal/register behavior and Japanese honorifics causing tone/regression issues.
- What we'll deliver next:
  1) A short benchmark summary (CSV) showing per-locale accuracy & hallucination rates across a recommended model shortlist.
  2) Prompt set v2 with locale-specific templates + test cases.
  3) Recommendations for model variants (quantized vs full precision) tuned for latency/cost tradeoffs.

Attachments: globex_multilingual_benchmarks.csv, redwood_promptset_v2.txt (sample prompts), eval_report_q2.pdf (methodology). Links to full evals in Drive below.

Recommended models from our initial pass:
- redwood-xt-1.3B-quant (best cost/latency for JP/SG internal routing)
- redwood-large-7B-8bit (balanced quality for DE/FR/ES)
- open-Llama2-13B-8bit (fallback for high-complexity threads where RDW-7B shows hallucination)

Next steps / asks:
- Anna: confirm the 10 representative German/French tickets you want in the regression set (share by EOD Thursday).
- Ravi: can you surface 5 high-priority APAC intents (Japanese/Korean) we should prioritize?
- Internally: David / Rishi, can you run the latency sweep on redwood-xt-1.3B-quant for JP tokenization and confirm prefix-cache behavior for chat contexts?

I'll follow up with a short Loom that walks through the CSV columns and our per-locale error breakdown.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Anna Schmidt <a.schmidt@globexretail.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 13:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (multilingual evals)

Hi Marissa --

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks good. A few clarifications: 

- I'll upload the 10 German/French tickets to the shared Drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleBenchmarks) by EOD Thursday. Prefer that we keep the test set representative of our high-severity returns (refunds, policy disputes).
- For German: please include formal + informal variants; we've seen the model switch register in the middle of conversations.
- For French: watch for second-person plural/formal usage (vous/tu) mistakes.

One ask on the benchmark CSV: can you add a "severity" column and a short example of expected agent reply style? That helps our CS validators score quality consistently.

Appreciate the quick Loom.

Best,
Anna
Head of Conversational Automation | Globex Retail
a.schmidt@globexretail.de
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Schmidt <a.schmidt@globexretail.de>, Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@apaccommerce.co.sg>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (multilingual evals)

Anna -- great, thanks. Two small updates based on your asks:

1) I added a "severity" column and an "expected_reply_style" short string to the CSV (see attached eval_report_q2.pdf for mapping).
2) Prompt set v2 includes locale templates for DE/FR/JP/KR and examples for formality handling (see redwood_promptset_v2.txt).

Rishi / David: looping you back in. For prioritization, Anna has requested that we preserve register (formal/informal) for DE and politeness/honorifics for JP. Can we do a quick calibration run:
- Metric targets: intent accuracy delta <= 3% vs SparkHelp baseline; hallucination <= 2% absolute; median latency <= 300ms for chat path.
- Suggested immediate experiment: redwood-large-7B-8bit + locale-specific prompt templates with prefix caching enabled.

Ravi -- are the APAC intents still the same list we discussed (returns, delivery exceptions, product guidance, order lookups, payments)? If yes, Marissa will add them to the APAC bucket for evaluation.

I'll set up a follow-up next Tuesday to review the first-pass per-locale confusion matrices.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: globex_multilingual_benchmarks.csv, redwood_promptset_v2.txt
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 13:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (multilingual evals)

Marissa / Rishi --

Quick internal note after skimming the CSV: good signal on per-locale F1, but two operational points we should confirm before demo: 

1) Tokenization differences: JP/KR tokenization increases request token counts substantially on some tickets. Rishi, can you run the quantized model latency sweep with the JP tokenizer and a 512-token chat context? We need concrete median and p95 numbers for redwood-xt-1.3B-quant vs redwood-large-7B-8bit.

2) Fallback policy: If redwood-7B produces a high hallucination score (>2%), we should automatically route to open-Llama2-13B-8bit for the high-severity tickets. Need to see cost delta for that fallback (approx).

Also Laura, make sure we flag the dataset for PII-scrubbing checks (Globex asked for examples; the CSV has a few masked ids but call this out).

Thanks - I'll take the latency sweep and share numbers by 3pm PT.

-David
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (multilingual evals)

David / team --

Running the JP tokenizer latency sweep now. Early results (local dev infra, small batch):
- redwood-xt-1.3B-quant: median 210ms, p95 460ms (512-token context, prefix cache cold)
- redwood-large-7B-8bit: median 320ms, p95 780ms
- open-Llama2-13B-8bit: median 580ms, p95 1.2s

Notes: prefix cache warm starts reduce medians by ~30-40ms on these runs. Quantized path looks promising for APAC routing where latency is critical; redwood-large-7B offers better raw quality for DE/FR but costs ~1.6x vs quant path. Fallback to 13B is feasible for high-severity tickets but will increase cost and p95 significantly.

I'll push the numeric sweep and cost delta to the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleBenchmarks) and tag the configs.

Rishi
Senior ML Engineer, Inference Optimization | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
